land.text: the western half of Tarumanagara, west of the Tarum (Citarum) River

predecessors.note: The Sunda page has no 670 date and puts the kingdom's 'established' year at 932 (the Kebon Kopi II inscription, 'dated 854 Saka (932 AD)'); 670 is the Galuh page's date for the division of Tarumanagara.

union.text: Pakuan Pajajaran, the capital razed in 1579

land.text: the west of Sunda, Pakuan included: 'razed and destroyed by the Sultanate of Banten in 1579'
the eastern Sunda land that Cliopatria gives to Cirebon in 1579

successors.note: Sumedang Larang 'joined the Cirebon Sultanate' under Prince Santri (1530-1578) and 'declared itself a sovereign state and separated from Cirebon' in 1585.

land.text: the Pajajaran inheritance that 'Prince Angkawijaya received ... in 1578 and was crowned king'

successors.note: No Cliopatria row (a Sumedang Larang entry would be a new state); the Sumedang page's infobox says independence 1529 and its text 1585.

capitals.name: Pakuan (Bogor)
capitals.note: Tarusbawa, after the Srivijayan attack, 'moved inland and founded a capital near the Cipakancilan river, near modern Bogor' (Tarumanagara page); the Sunda page gives Pakuan and Kawali without years for the early centuries.

capitals.name: Kawali (Ciamis)
capitals.note: Niskala Wastu Kancana (1371) renovated the Kawali palace and built defences round Kawali; Kawali was the seat until 1482. Also Galuh's capital (Galuh page).

capitals.name: Pakuan Pajajaran (Bogor)
capitals.note: Jayadewata 'moved the government seat from Kawali back to Pakuan in 1482'; razed 1579.

rulers.name: Sri Jayabhupati
rulers.note: Named in the Sanghyang Tapak inscription of 952 Saka (1030); the table's earlier names are omitted.

rulers.name: Prabu Guru Dharmasiksa
rulers.note: The page's table gives 1175-1297, a 122-year span that probably merges reigns.

correction.text: Sunda, the western half of Tarumanagara west of the Citarum: Cliopatria's 674 shape held from 670

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Sunda row starts 674, but the Galuh page has 'In 670, Tarumanagara was divided into the Sunda Kingdom (west) and the Galuh Kingdom (east), separated by the Tarum (Citarum) River'. The shape is Cliopatria's 674 shape unchanged.

26,774 km2 for 674-723: Banten, Jakarta and the Bogor country west of the Citarum, consistent with the division at the Tarum (Citarum) River. The Tarumanagara page says 'coastal Banten and Jakarta areas came under Srivijayan control after the invasion', which Cliopatria's Sunda shape still draws as Sunda's (its Srivijaya shape of 692 holds no Banten or Jakarta cell); unresolved. The Sunda page gives no area; its 'present-day Banten, Jakarta, West Java, Lampung, and western Central Java' is the kingdom at its widest.

correction.text: Sunda alone, west of the Citarum, as in the shape of 741: no page opened puts Galuh inside Sunda in 724-731

keyframe_review.note: 62,498 km2 (Sunda plus Galuh) for 724-731. The Galuh page has Purbasora killed in Sanjaya's invasion of 723 and Premanadikusuma 'appointed by Sanjaya' on the Galuh throne 723-732, so the eastern half is Galuh's under Mataram, not Sunda's; the Sunda page is silent on 723. Only the Carita Parahyangan (Sanjaya of Mataram page: 'the Sundanese king and hero of Galuh', 'romanticized and mythical') makes Sanjaya a Sunda king.

correction.text: Sunda alone, as in the shape of 741

keyframe_review.note: 121,225 km2 for 732-740: Cliopatria adds Sanjaya's Mataram (Central and East Java) and Galuh to Sunda. The Galuh page has Tamperan Barmawijaya, Sanjaya's son, on the Galuh throne 732-739 until Manarah killed him, and the Mataram page dates the Canggal inscription, the first account of Mataram, to 732: Mataram and Galuh have their own dossiers, and Sunda stays west of the Citarum.
26,774 km2 for 741-824: Sunda alone, west of the Citarum, with Galuh restored under Manarah (739-783 in the page's table) and Mataram separate. Cliopatria's 741 fits Manarah's accession in 739.

unverified: page budget. 62,041 km2 for 825-895: Cliopatria joins Galuh to Sunda. The Galuh page's table of kings ends with Guruminda Sang Minisri (783-799) and says Galuh was 'absorbed into the Sunda kingdom' in the 10th century (approximate); it gives nothing for 825.
unverified: page budget. 26,774 km2 for 896-1027: Sunda alone again. No page opened separates the kingdoms in the 10th century; the Galuh page puts their union in that century.

unverified: page budget. 62,041 km2 for 1028-1293: Sunda and Galuh united. The Sunda page lists Sri Jayabhupati (952 Saka, 1030) and Prabu Guru Dharmasiksa (1175-1297) but nothing on borders; the Galuh page has Galuh's capital at Kawali by the 13th century.

62,270 km2 for 1294-1474, 229 km2 more than before. The Sunda page: 'the eastern border of the kingdom was the Pemali River' (Bujangga Manik), vassal land from Pasar Talo (Bengkulu) to Jatimalang (Purworejo), and Tome Pires (1513): the kingdom 'ends at the river Cimanuk'. The shape reaches 110.0E, beyond the Pemali (about 109.0E) to the Serayu, which the Galuh page names as Galuh's eastern limit. The Bubat battle of 1357 moves no border.
26,774 km2 for 1475-1481: the table says Niskala Wastu Kancana 'split Sunda and Galuh between his two sons' (1475) and lists a 'Twin equal kingdom of Sunda and Galuh'.

54,102 km2 for 1482-1518: Sunda and Galuh rejoined under Jayadewata at Pakuan, less Cirebon, which 'proclaimed itself as a sovereign independent state' in 1482 (chronogram 2 April 1482). 54,102 plus Cirebon's 7,967 km2 is 62,069, close to the 62,270 km2 of the earlier union.

53,873 km2 for 1519-1528, 229 km2 less than 1482; no page explains the sliver. By 1522 'the Portuguese were ready to form a coalition with the King of Sunda' (Sunda page); in 1512-1515 'the port of Banten still belonged to the Hindu Kingdom of Sunda' (Banten page).

correction.text: Sunda without the harbour of Sunda Kalapa (Jakarta), captured for Demak in 1527

keyframe_review.note: 44,266 km2 for 1529-1571: Banten leaves (infobox 'Syarif Hidayatullah conquered Banten: 1526'; Hasanuddin's operation 'likely' 1527, Banten page) and Demak takes Sunda Kalapa ('Fatahillah ... managed to capture the Sunda Kalapa harbour', renamed Jayakarta). Cliopatria dates the loss of Banten to 1529 and keeps Jakarta inside.

union.text: Pakuan Pajajaran, the capital razed in 1579

correction.text: The eastern Sunda land of 1572 plus Pakuan Pajajaran (Bogor), the capital until it was razed in 1579

keyframe_review.note: 22,146 km2 for 1572-1578 drops the whole west, Pakuan (Bogor) included. The Sunda page has Pakuan, the capital from 1482, 'razed and destroyed by the Sultanate of Banten in 1579' and the kingdom falling apart 'particularly after 1576 due to constant pressure from Banten'; the Banten page's sentence that at Hasanuddin's death in 1570 Banten 'comprised all of Sunda' except Cirebon and Sumedang Larang conflicts with that and is read as the conquest in progress.

region.text: Sunda, the western half of Tarumanagara, west of the Citarum

ledger.note: 670: Tarumanagara divides and Sunda appears in the west. 'In 670, Tarumanagara was divided into the Sunda Kingdom (west) and the Galuh Kingdom (east), separated by the Tarum (Citarum) River'; Galuh's infobox dates the separation to 669. The Sunda page's own infobox says 'Kingdom established: 932 AD' (the Kebon Kopi II inscription, 'dated 854 Saka (932 AD)', the earliest reference to Sunda as a kingdom).

region.text: the Galuh land east of the Citarum

ledger.note: c. 825: Galuh is joined to Sunda (Cliopatria's year; the pages opened are silent on 825). The Galuh page says Galuh 'was absorbed into the Sunda kingdom' in the 10th century (approximate).

region.text: the Galuh land east of the Citarum

ledger.note: c. 896: Galuh stands apart again (Cliopatria's year; page silent).

region.text: the Galuh land east of the Citarum

ledger.note: c. 1028: Sunda and Galuh are one again (Cliopatria's year; page silent). The Galuh page: 'the two later formed the United Kingdom of Sunda and Galuh'.
1371: the court goes to Kawali. Niskala Wastu Kancana 'ascended the throne. The Kawali palace was renovated and defences were built around Kawali'; the page has Kawali as the seat until 1482.
1475: Niskala Wastu Kancana divides the realm. The table says he 'split Sunda and Galuh between his two sons'; Susuk Tunggal takes Sunda and Ningrat Kancana Galuh.
1482: Sunda and Galuh are reunited. Galuh's infobox: 'Unification of Sunda and Galuh: 1482'; the Sunda page lists Jayadewata as ruler of 'Sunda and Galuh' from Pakuan.
1482: the court returns to Pakuan. Jayadewata 'moved the government seat from Kawali back to Pakuan in 1482'.

region.text: Cirebon, the port of Muara Jati and its hinterland

ledger.note: 1482: Cirebon breaks away. Cirebon 'proclaimed itself as a sovereign independent state', the chronogram corresponding to 2 April 1482 (its infobox says 1479); the Banten page has 'proclaiming independence of Cirebon from Sunda' in 1482.

region.text: the port of Banten and its hinterland

ledger.note: 1527: Banten falls. Infobox 'Syarif Hidayatullah conquered Banten: 1526'; 'It was likely that his son Hasanudin commanded this military operation in 1527'; Banten was then held as a province under Cirebon. Cliopatria's Banten shape starts 1529.

1527: Sunda Kalapa falls to Demak. 'Fatahillah managed to capture the Sunda Kalapa harbour', renamed Jayakarta, after the Sunda-Portuguese coalition of 1522; Surawisesa made peace with Demak and Cirebon in 1531 (Banten page).

minus.text: Pakuan Pajajaran, the capital razed in 1579

region.text: the western Sunda land: Banten, Tangerang and the lowlands, Pakuan excepted

ledger.note: 1570s: Banten takes western Sunda (the year is Cliopatria's 1572; the pages date no conquest of the west). The Sunda page: the kingdom 'has fallen apart, particularly after 1576 due to constant pressure from Banten' and 'finally collapsed completely in 1579'; an earlier Banten attack under Hasanuddin 'captured and razed the capital'. The Banten page has Banten comprising 'all of Sunda, except for Cirebon and Sumedang Larang' at Hasanuddin's death in 1570, which the Sunda page's 1579 contradicts.

region.text: Pakuan Pajajaran, the capital razed in 1579

ledger.note: 1579: Pakuan Pajajaran is razed. The capital was 'razed and destroyed by the Sultanate of Banten in 1579'.

union.text: Pakuan Pajajaran, the capital razed in 1579

region.text: the last Sunda land: Pakuan and the east

ledger.note: 1579: the Sunda Kingdom ends. The page says it 'finally collapsed completely in 1579'; its infobox gives the successors Banten, Cirebon and Sumedang Larang, and Prince Angkawijaya had received the Pajajaran inheritance in 1578 (Sumedang page).

wars.name: Battle of Bubat
wars.outcome: Majapahit victory: the Sunda king Maharaja Linggabuana and almost the whole royal party killed at Bubat square; 'It is possible that Sunda became vassalized by Majapahit after this battle' and it 'ultimately regained independence probably before the Regreg War'. No territory is reported lost.
wars.note: Majapahit page: Gajah Mada 'saw this event as an opportunity to demand Sunda's submission to Majapahit overlordship'. Not drawn as a vassalage: the page itself calls it only possible.

wars.name: Demak-Cirebon conquest of Banten and Sunda Kalapa

zones.text: the port of Banten and Sunda Kalapa

wars.outcome: Banten and Sunda Kalapa pass from Sunda; Surawisesa signed a peace treaty with Demak and Cirebon in 1531.
wars.note: Triggered by the 1522 Portuguese-Sunda coalition; Banten infobox 1526, body 1527.

wars.name: Banten conquest of Pakuan Pajajaran
wars.outcome: Pakuan razed in 1579 and the Sunda Kingdom ends; Sumedang Larang inherits the crown in 1578 and Cirebon the east.
wars.note: The Sunda page also has Hasanuddin attacking and razing Pakuan in the 1550s.

certainty.note: The pages give river lines (Citarum, Pemali, Cimanuk) and vassal reaches, never a surveyed frontier.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Sunda Kingdom' (674-1578, 13 shapes) is kept as ONE state, not split: the pages give one continuous Sunda line from Tarusbawa's Sunda to Raja Mulya (1579), and the Galuh Kingdom has its own Cliopatria row. The 26,774 km2 / 62,041 km2 alternation is Sunda alone versus Sunda plus Galuh; the same kingdom with Galuh joined. The shapes 825, 896 and 1028 rest on no dated page ('unverified: page budget'; the Galuh page says only that Galuh was absorbed in the 10th century). Start 670 is the Galuh page's date for the division of Tarumanagara; the Sunda page's infobox says 'established 932' (earliest inscription naming the kingdom). End 1579 against Cliopatria's 1578. Cliopatria's 724-740 rows put Sanjaya's Mataram inside the Sunda row: corrected to Sunda alone (the Mataram and Galuh dossiers carry those lands). The Pakuan (Bogor) capital is kept inside the 1572-1578 shape against Cliopatria. Disagreements: Banten page (Banten comprised all Sunda at Hasanuddin's death in 1570) against the Sunda page (Pakuan razed 1579); Cirebon independence 1479 (infobox) against 1482; Sunda Kalapa fall 1527 against Cliopatria keeping Jakarta to 1571. The Bubat battle of 1357 is not drawn as vassalage (the page says only 'possible'). Counterparts without a dossier: sumedang-larang (1578/1585-1620). Gazetteer names wanted: river Citarum, Cimanuk, Pemali (Brebes); places Kawali, Pakuan (Bogor), Sunda Kalapa; region Priangan/Parahyangan (Sumedang country). No infobox area to compare. All nine pages of the budget were opened.
